scope.geography: United States; Cleveland/Ohio prioritized when a sufficiently strong match is available
scope.selection_rule: Current actionable roles only; stale or expired postings excluded from this snapshot.

jobs.title: Associate Staff Scientist (Intestinal Organoids)
jobs.company_info: CuSTOM Accelerator combines intestinal organoids, stem-cell biology, tissue engineering, automation and translational human-model development.

salary.note: No salary listed on official posting.

jobs.posting_status: Active official employer posting with Apply button
jobs.job_description: Lead development, optimization and characterization of iPSC-derived intestinal organoids for IBD, therapeutic discovery, predictive toxicology and regenerative medicine, including scalable/automated workflows.
key_must_have_requirements: Stem-cell, intestinal, tissue-engineering or advanced in vitro model background
jobs.why_good_match: The strongest Ohio match: intestinal organoids, IBD, tissue engineering, confocal/high-content imaging, transcriptomics, single-cell analysis and MPS all map directly to current expertise.
likely_gaps: iPSC-derived intestinal organoid experience is less extensive than adult patient-derived organoid experience
jobs.tailor: Lead with patient-derived intestinal organoids and Crohn's chips, then scRNA-seq, confocal/IF and engineering; explicitly position adult-stem-cell expertise as a foundation for expanding into iPSC systems.
jobs.immediate_action: Apply now and use the interview to test first-author ownership, grant participation, promotion path and how much platform leadership the role actually carries.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Associate — Gastrointestinal Host Immune-Microbiome Organ-on-Chip
jobs.company_info: The Jalili Lab and Connecticut Children's GI collaboration is building in vitro gastrointestinal host-immune-microbiome models for inflammatory disease and therapeutic development.

salary.note: Salary not reliably surfaced in current listing.

jobs.job_description: Develop gastrointestinal host-immune-microbiome culture models using organoid engineering, organ-on-chip, microfluidics and microbiome science for Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis and related inflammatory disorders.
key_must_have_requirements: Interest/experience in organoids, microfluidics, organ-on-chip, microbiome or intestinal inflammation
jobs.why_good_match: Topic overlap is nearly exact: Crohn's/IBD, intestinal organoids, host-microbiome interactions and organ-on-chip. Unlike staying in the same lab, it would add an explicit immune compartment and a new institutional network.
likely_gaps: Immune-model depth may be less developed than epithelial/microbiome expertise
Because technical overlap is so high, the postdoc must provide genuinely new scientific ownership rather than simply repeating existing methods
jobs.tailor: Lead with susceptibility-exposure Crohn's work, patient-derived epithelium, microbiota co-culture and scRNA-seq; frame immune integration as the next mechanistic layer you want to acquire.
jobs.immediate_action: Contact the PI/team now and ask what immune component, independent hypothesis and first-author ownership would distinguish this postdoc from your doctoral work.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Fellow – NHP Immunology and Organ Chips
jobs.company_info: The Wyss team uses Organ Chips to compare human and NHP adaptive immunity and radiation toxicity with spatial omics and functional data.
jobs.term: One-year term with possibility of extension

salary.note: Harvard postdoctoral scale based on years post-PhD.

jobs.posting_status: Official Wyss page remains live; encouraged application date has passed
jobs.job_description: Use Organ Chips, spatial omics and functional assays to study adaptive immunity, vaccination and radiation toxicity across human and NHP systems, with pharma/regulatory exposure.
key_must_have_requirements: Strong collaborative analysis and publication skills
jobs.why_good_match: Radiation toxicity plus Organ Chips is unusually specific to radiation-on-chip experience, while spatial omics and regulatory/pharma interaction add meaningful breadth.
jobs.tailor: Open with radiation-on-chip, DNA damage/ROS/barrier assays and Organ Chip engineering; present scRNA/omics as evidence of computational adaptability rather than claiming NHP expertise.
jobs.immediate_action: Submit immediately while the official posting remains live and send a concise note connecting radiation-chip experience to the project.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Researcher or Staff Scientist — Integrated Microphysiological Systems
jobs.company_info: The Ouyang group develops integrated microphysiological systems and bio-integrated microsystems at the engineering/medicine interface.

salary.note: Not listed on lab opportunity page.

jobs.posting_status: Lab page currently states it is seeking postdoctoral researcher or staff scientist candidates for integrated MPS
jobs.job_description: Develop integrated microphysiological systems within a bio-integrated microsystems lab spanning microdevices, sensing and biomedical engineering.
jobs.why_good_match: This would deepen the engineering side—microfabrication, device integration, sensing and MPS—rather than simply repeating GI biology.
likely_gaps: Exact project scope and funding terms require direct discussion
jobs.tailor: Lead with porous PDMS membrane fabrication, multiplex fluidics, pump/actuator design and organ-chip validation; include a visual engineering portfolio.
jobs.immediate_action: Contact Prof. Ouyang directly with a one-page research-fit note and ask whether the staff-scientist or postdoc track best matches an incoming PhD.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Research Associate — Host-Microbe Interactions (Kumar Lab)
jobs.company_info: The Kumar Lab studies how xenobiotics and host immune factors remodel the gut microbiome and intestinal homeostasis using omics, anaerobic microbiology and mechanistic models.
jobs.job_description: Lead mechanistic studies of drug-microbiome-immune interactions using clinical/high-throughput omics, anaerobic culturomics, bacterial genetics and in vivo models of intestinal homeostasis and disease.
key_must_have_requirements: Ability to lead independent mechanistic projects
Interest in host-microbiome and intestinal disease
jobs.why_good_match: Excellent biological fit and a chance to gain anaerobic bacterial genetics/culturomics—the microbial causal-manipulation layer that an epithelial chip alone cannot provide.
likely_gaps: Bacterial genetics and gnotobiotic/in vivo modeling
jobs.tailor: Lead with CD-versus-FMT microbiota phenotypes, shotgun metagenomics/HUMAnN and epithelial redox biology; explicitly pitch the desire to move from community association to causal microbial mechanisms.
jobs.immediate_action: Apply while the listing is fresh; position this as a deliberate microbiome-mechanism expansion rather than abandoning organ-chip engineering.

jobs.title: Assistant Project Scientist — 3D Bioprinters, Bioreactors and AI for Bioprinting
jobs.company: University of California San Diego, Jacobs School of Engineering
jobs.company_info: The project focuses on light-based 3D bioprinter development, bioreactor hardware/software and machine-learning optimization of bioprinting.

salary.note: Salary not surfaced in search result.

jobs.posting_status: Official UCSD recruitment page active; published September 21
jobs.job_description: Develop DLP-based 3D bioprinters, bioreactors, associated hardware/software and machine-learning methods for process optimization.
key_must_have_requirements: PhD in engineering or related field
jobs.why_good_match: Strategically attractive because it would turn current 3D printing, microfabrication and fluidic-device work into a much deeper biofabrication/automation platform skill set.
jobs.tailor: Make the engineering portfolio central: custom fabrication, PDMS membrane process development, flow-control hardware, 3D printing and iterative device troubleshooting; be explicit about the ML/DLP gaps.
jobs.immediate_action: Apply only as a high-upside stretch and use the research statement to propose how organ-chip fabrication and controlled perfusion could connect to automated biofabrication.
